instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Rows where hours is above the average
output: SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE hours > (SELECT AVG(hours) FROM tasks);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Row with the highest hours
output: SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE hours = (SELECT MAX(hours) FROM tasks);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Row with the lowest hours
output: SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE hours = (SELECT MIN(hours) FROM tasks);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Rows where id is in a subquery from tasks
output: SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE id IN (SELECT DISTINCT id FROM tasks);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Rows where id is not in the set of values 1 and 2
output: SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE id NOT IN (1, 2);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Use EXISTS to find rows where a id appears more than once
output: SELECT * FROM tasks t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tasks t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id GROUP BY t2.id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Subquery in SELECT returning count per id
output: SELECT t.*, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tasks t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id) AS cnt FROM tasks t;

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Rows where hours > the maximum of project_id plus 100 in subquery
output: SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE hours > ((SELECT MAX(hours) FROM tasks) + 100);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Second highest hours using subquery
output: SELECT MAX(hours) FROM tasks WHERE hours < (SELECT MAX(hours) FROM tasks);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Correlated subquery: rows whose hours is above the avg of their id
output: SELECT * FROM tasks t WHERE hours > (SELECT AVG(hours) FROM tasks t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Columns where hours is greater than average in their group
output: SELECT * FROM tasks t WHERE hours >= (SELECT AVG(hours) FROM tasks t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Derived table returning count per id
output: SELECT sub.id, sub.cnt FROM (SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM tasks GROUP BY id) sub WHERE sub.cnt > 2;

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Subquery filtering rows with ANY operator
output: SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE hours = ANY (SELECT hours FROM tasks WHERE hours < 50);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Subquery filtering rows with ALL operator
output: SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE hours > ALL (SELECT AVG(hours) FROM tasks);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Scalar subquery for a single value
output: SELECT (SELECT AVG(hours) FROM tasks) AS avg_val;

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Rows matching set from a subquery using IN
output: SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM tasks GROUP BY id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Largest value strictly less than the global maximum
output: SELECT hours FROM tasks ORDER BY hours DESC LIMIT 1 OFFSET 1;

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Nested subquery: top values per group based on derived ranking
output: SELECT t.* FROM tasks t WHERE t.hours = (SELECT MAX(hours) FROM tasks t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Rows where project_id not present in a sub table
output: SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE project_id NOT IN (SELECT project_id FROM tasks WHERE hours > 90);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Subquery used to compare against the overall total
output: SELECT id, SUM(hours) AS part FROM tasks GROUP BY id HAVING SUM(hours) > (SELECT AVG(hours) FROM tasks);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Use a subquery to compute rolling reference count
output: SELECT t.id, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tasks t2 WHERE t2.id <= t.id) AS running FROM tasks t;

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
EXISTS correlated check to its own table values
output: SELECT * FROM tasks t WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tasks t2 WHERE t2.id = t.id AND t2.hours > t.hours);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Subquery comparing to the minimum plus a constant
output: SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE hours > (SELECT MIN(hours) FROM tasks) + 10;

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Subquery returning rows for a top slice group
output: SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE hours IN (SELECT hours FROM tasks ORDER BY hours DESC LIMIT 5);

instruction:
Schema: tasks(id, project_id, hours)
Subquery joining a derived aggregate
output: SELECT t.* FROM tasks t JOIN (SELECT id, MAX(hours) mx FROM tasks GROUP BY id) a ON a.id = t.id AND a.mx = t.hours;
